How to price a multi-device backflow test visit

A single-device visit is the easy case. Most real property visits are not: a strip mall can carry six assemblies across its fire lines, domestic service, and irrigation meter, and a hand-priced job is where the multi-device discount, the per-device filing fee, and a retest line most often go wrong.

The rule, in one line

First device at full price. Every device after it on the same visit gets your additional-device discount. Every device — discounted or not, passed or failed — gets the per-device filing fee. Any device that fails also gets the retest fee. Add your one-time travel fee once for the whole visit, not once per device.

Worked example: a 6-device strip mall visit

Three domestic and fire-line RPZ assemblies, two irrigation double-checks, and one landscape PVB, with a 20% additional-device discount, a $15 report-filing fee per device, a $40 one-time travel fee, and a $35 retest fee for the one device that fails:

DeviceTest feeDiscounted feeFilingRetestLine total
1. Domestic RPZ — first device$65.00$65.00 (no discount)$15.00—$80.00
2. Fire line RPZ #1$65.00$52.00$15.00—$67.00
3. Fire line RPZ #2 — failed$65.00$52.00$15.00$35.00$102.00
4. Irrigation double-check #1$55.00$44.00$15.00—$59.00
5. Irrigation double-check #2$55.00$44.00$15.00—$59.00
6. Landscape PVB$45.00$36.00$15.00—$51.00
SubtotalAmount
Testing (discount saved $57.00 across 5 devices)$293.00
Report filing (6 devices × $15.00)$90.00
Retest (1 device)$35.00
Travel (one-time)$40.00
Total$458.00
Average per device$76.33

Compare that to pricing the visit at a flat per-device rate. Six devices at the first device's own $65 rate, with no filing fee, no travel fee, and no retest line, would quote $390.00 — $68.00 below this visit's real $458.00 total, before whatever the filing fee and retest were actually worth on their own ($125.00 between them). The gap is not the discount; it is everything a flat per-device number has no line for.

Common questions

How do I price a property visit with more than one backflow device?

Charge the first device full price, since it carries the trip's travel and setup cost. Apply your additional-device discount to every device after it. Add your report-filing fee to every device regardless of the discount, since most water utilities require a separate submitted report per device. Add a retest fee for any device that fails, and your one-time travel fee once for the whole visit.

Does the multi-device discount apply to the first device too?

No. The discount reflects travel and setup time shared across the visit, and the first device is what pays for that time. Discounting it too would undercharge every single-device visit's worth of setup cost baked into the trip.

Does the filing fee still apply to a device that gets the multi-device discount, or one that failed?

Yes, both. The filing fee covers the report a water utility requires per device, which is separate paperwork whether or not that device's testing rate was discounted, and whether it passed or failed. In the worked example on this page, all six devices carry the filing fee, including the one that failed.

How is a retest priced if a device fails?

This calculator assumes the retest happens on the same visit, billed at a flat retest fee with no added travel charge. If a failed device needs a separate return trip — waiting on a repair part, for instance — add that trip's own travel fee separately rather than folding it into the retest fee.

What does the calculator not know?

It only totals the fee schedule you enter against the devices you list. It does not test anything, does not determine whether a device passed or failed, and does not know your water utility's required report form, filing deadline, or device-type requirements — those vary by state and by utility. Confirm them against your local cross-connection control program before invoicing or filing.

No warranty. This page and the linked calculator apply the fee schedule and discount you configure to numbers you supply; they are not legal, engineering, or regulatory advice. You are responsible for verifying anything here against your own fee schedule and your water utility's requirements. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for any loss or damage arising from its use.

Nothing leaves your browser. The calculator this page links to runs entirely client-side; nothing you enter is uploaded anywhere. The worked example above uses illustrative figures, not a claim about what any water utility or tester actually charges.

Common questions

How much should I charge to test multiple backflow devices at one property?

Most testers charge full price for the first device on a visit, then a reduced fee for each additional device on the same property — since the travel and setup time is already covered by the first device's fee — plus a per-device report-filing fee, since most water utilities require a separate submitted report for each assembly.

Why does the report-filing fee apply to every device, even with a multi-device discount?

The multi-device discount reflects shared travel and setup time on one visit, not shared paperwork. Most water utilities require a separate test report submitted for every device — passed or failed — so the filing fee is charged per device regardless of the testing discount.

How should a failed device be billed?

This calculator assumes a failed device is retested on the same visit, billed at a flat retest fee with no added travel charge. If a failed device needs a separate return trip — for example waiting on a repair part — add that trip's travel fee separately; this calculator only totals the fee schedule you enter, it does not schedule or track return visits.

Does this tell me if a device passed or failed, or what my water utility requires?

No. This calculator only totals your own fee schedule against the devices on one job. It does not test anything, does not determine pass or fail, and does not know your water utility's required report form, filing deadline, or device-type requirements — those vary by state and by utility. Confirm those against your local cross-connection control program.

No. It applies the fee schedule and discount you configure to the devices you enter — it is not legal, engineering, or regulatory advice, and it does not replace checking your water utility's own backflow-testing requirements.

This calculator vs. Jobber

Two different shapes: Jobber is an account-based platform for running a testing or plumbing company's whole operation, including scheduling the visit and invoicing the customer once a price already exists. This page is a free, private worksheet for one question -- what should today's visit cost, given the devices on it, the multi-device discount, the per-device filing fee, and any retest fee, before you quote it.

What each one is for

Jobber is a field service management platform used by home and trade service businesses -- plumbing, backflow testing, HVAC, electrical and general contracting among them -- to run client management and online quoting, scheduling and dispatch, invoicing and online payments, and a client-facing hub, tied to one account used on an ongoing basis across every visit the company runs. Jobber's own site is not reachable from this session to confirm today's specific feature list, plan names, or pricing, so only its well-documented identity and category are stated here: nothing about it is invented, and no dollar figure for it appears on this page. Public descriptions of that kind of field service software describe scheduling a visit, dispatching a tester, and invoicing and collecting payment once a price already exists; none describe applying a multi-device discount to every device after the first while keeping a per-device filing fee on the discounted or failed ones -- which is what this calculator does.

This calculator does none of what Jobber does. It does not manage a customer list, schedule a visit, or collect a payment. It takes the devices on one property visit, applies the per-device test fee with the multi-device discount to devices after the first, adds the per-device municipal filing fee and any retest fee for a device that failed, and turns that into an itemized total for the visit -- then a plain-text breakdown to paste into an invoice or work order.

This tool needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off.

Common questions

Should I use this calculator or Jobber?

They do different jobs, and a backflow tester of any size will likely end up touching both eventually. Jobber is a field service management platform used across home and trade service businesses -- plumbing and backflow testing among them -- to run client management and online quoting, scheduling and dispatch, invoicing and online payments, and a client hub, tied to one account used on an ongoing basis across every visit the company runs. It runs free in any browser, keeps no account, and uploads nothing you type. A tester already scheduling visits, managing a customer list, and invoicing and collecting payment across an ongoing business is better served by Jobber or a comparable field service platform; a tester who wants an instant, private, itemized total for the devices on today's visit is in the right place here.

This calculator vs. a spreadsheet

A backflow tester who prices multi-device jobs more than once usually ends up with a spreadsheet: full price for the first device, a discounted rate for each additional one, a filing fee per device, and a retest line for anything that failed. That sheet is correct if every row's formula is right and stays right every time a device is added or removed. This page names no specific product -- it compares against the generic method of pricing a job in a spreadsheet or by hand, not a competing calculator.

What each one is for

A spreadsheet can price this correctly, and many testers already have one. What it does not do on its own is stop a discount formula from being applied to the wrong row after a device is added, or catch a filing fee left off a device that failed.

This calculator applies the first-device-full-price rule, the multi-device discount, the per-device filing fee, and the retest fee to the devices you enter, shows every line separately, and lets you copy the full breakdown as a plain-text record for an invoice or work order -- no formula to write or re-check.

QuestionWhere to answer it
Can I price a multi-device job in a spreadsheet?Yes -- if the discount and filing-fee rows stay right as devices change.
Does the discount apply to the first device?No -- only to devices after the first, the mistake this calculator's FAQ and this page both call out.
Does the filing fee still apply to a discounted or failed device?Yes -- filing is per device regardless of the testing discount or pass/fail result.
Can I hand someone the full breakdown without re-deriving it?This calculator's copy-breakdown output, not a screenshot of a formula bar.
Does either one know my water utility's requirements?Neither -- both only total the fee schedule you enter.

Common questions

Can a spreadsheet price a multi-device backflow test job?

Yes, with the right formula: full price for the first device, a discounted rate for every device after it, a per-device filing fee added regardless of the discount, and a retest fee for any device that failed. The arithmetic is not hard — getting every row's discount and filing fee right, and keeping it right as devices are added or removed, is where a hand-built sheet most often drifts.

Where does a hand-built backflow fee sheet usually go wrong?

Two places: applying the multi-device discount to the first device by mistake (it should stay full price, since it carries the trip's travel and setup cost), and forgetting the filing fee still applies to a discounted or failed device, since most water utilities require a separate report per device regardless of the testing rate charged.

What does a spreadsheet not check for you?

Whether a copied formula still points at the right row after a device was added or removed, and whether the filing fee and retest fee were both included for every device that needed them. A calculator built for this one job runs the same formula every time and shows the full per-device breakdown so the total is checkable by eye.

Does either one know my water utility's requirements?

No. Both this calculator and a spreadsheet only total the fee schedule you enter. Neither knows your water utility's required report form, filing deadline, or device-type requirements — confirm those against your local cross-connection control program before invoicing or filing.

Is anything I enter uploaded anywhere?

No. The calculator this page links to runs entirely in your browser; nothing you enter is uploaded.
